title: When the Monsoon Turns
premise: Theo Oyelaran, a salvage diver hiding from a past debt, is hired to quietly strip a wreck in a monsoon-flooded river delta—until she recovers a chest bearing the seal of a nation that no longer exists, drawing the attention of the navy officers who sank it and the smugglers who want its contents. Forced to flee downriver with Amara Sen, a cartographer whose brother died on that wreck, Theo must navigate flooded channels, betrayals, and her own guilt to reach a port where the chest can expose a decades-old atrocity. In the climax, Theo trades the compass—her last link to her drowned father—to buy passage through a naval blockade, and she and Amara deliver the evidence at the cost of the boat and nearly their lives. The story ends with the monsoon breaking, the truth published, and Theo choosing, for the first time, to stay visible.
about_author: Mirabel Halloran is a former maritime archaeologist who spent six years documenting river wrecks across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about water, memory, and the people history tries to submerge.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Diving alone on a navy-restricted wreck in the swollen delta, Theo catalogs cargo while dodging patrol boats, establishing her debt to a salvage broker and her careful invisibility. The emotional beat is wary competence masking loneliness; she treats the river as an employer, never a home.

chapters.title: A Seal Out of Water
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Deep in the hull she finds a sealed chest stamped with the crest of Vessania, a nation erased from maps thirty years ago. When a patrol boat arrives too quickly, she realizes someone was watching. The beat shifts from routine to dread: the river has stopped being neutral territory.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara Sen confronts Theo at the dock, recognizing the seal from her missing brother's letters—he crewed on that wreck before it 'sank.' She offers Theo money for the chest; Theo refuses, but the broker sells them both out. The beat is reluctant alliance born of shared grief.

chapters.title: Running Before the Rain
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. With smugglers burning the dock behind them, Theo and Amara escape downriver on Theo's leaking boat as the first true monsoon squall hits. They open the chest: documents naming officers who scuttled a refugee ship. The beat is adrenaline and dawning purpose—their survival now has stakes beyond themselves.

chapters.title: What the Flood Remembers
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Sheltering in a drowned village, Amara reads the documents aloud and reconstructs her brother's final voyage, while Theo deflects questions about her own father's disappearance at sea. The beat is intimacy through confession deferred; two kinds of drowning surface between them.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The broker catches up with an offer: the chest for forgiveness of Theo's debt—and protection from the navy captain hunting them. Theo nearly accepts, then learns the broker plans to sell the documents back to the men they implicate. The beat is temptation and refusal; Theo chooses duty over safety for the first time.

chapters.title: Narrow Waters
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. A cat-and-mouse chase through mangrove channels as the navy closes one exit after another. Amara uses her old survey charts to thread a route marked on no official map—her brother's secret channel. The beat is trust forged under fire; Amara stops being cargo and becomes co-pilot of the escape.

chapters.title: The Captain's Offer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cornered at a fueling station, Captain Reyes offers Theo amnesty and her debt erased if she surrenders the chest, revealing he knew her father—and let him die. Shattered, Theo pretends to consider. The beat is rage weaponized into resolve; the personal wound becomes the reason to finish.

chapters.title: Compass Point
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, climax. To slip the blockade at Port Calloway, Theo needs a pilot who demands her father's compass as payment—the last thing she owns of him. She hands it over, guides the boat through mined shallows under fire, and reaches the press office with Amara as the boat sinks beneath them. The beat is sacrifice transmuted: the compass points her to truth instead of home.

chapters.title: After the Rain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. The documents break open an inquiry; Reyes is arrested, the broker vanishes, and the refugee dead are named publicly. Theo, debt-free but unmoored, prepares to disappear again—until Amara asks her to stay and help map the channel her brother died protecting. The beat is quiet arrival: Theo chooses visibility, love, and a place on the water that finally feels like hers.
